Cognition, the startup behind the autonomous AI software engineer Devin, said it has crossed $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate, according to [a post on the company's blog](https://cognition.com/blog/1b-run-rate). "Today, Cognition crossed $1B in annualized revenue run rate," the company wrote in the post, published under the byline The Cognition Team.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 735 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Neutral, factual tone throughout; no editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and their gzip snapshots' sha256 hashes match the manifest (source-0.html.gz = cognition.com/blog/1b-run-rate; source-1.html.gz = techcrunch.com 2026-09-08 $48B valuation piece; source-2.html.gz = cognition.com/blog/series-e). I decompressed and read all three verbatim (not re-fetched). source-0: confirms the exact quote 'Today, Cognition crossed $1B in annualized revenue run rate.', the 'January 2024' founding quote, the customer names GE Aerospace/Rivian/Rohlik/Exa, the 'The Cognition Team' byline, and the 09.25.26 publish date, plus 'belongs to our customers' (meta description) / 'belongs to them' (body) supporting the article's paraphrase 'belongs to' its customers. source-1 (TechCrunch): confirms '$2 billion at a $48 billion valuation', the prior '$26 billion valuation' four months earlier, the investor list 'Andreessen Horowitz, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir', the verbatim run-rate phrase 'grown from $492 million to $900 million', the Cursor comparison ('$2 billion' revenue at the time of its funding talks before its '$60 billion' SpaceX sale), the verbatim 'hundreds of millions of dollars annually' server-lease cost, and 'Founded in 2024 by math prodigy Scott Wu, Cognition counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi among its major enterprise customers.' source-2 (Cognition Series E post): confirms the page's own <title> is 'Do it all with Devin: Announcing our Series E | Cognition' and the body quote 'Since our last round in May, Cognition's run-rate revenue has grown from $492M to almost $900M.', published 2026-09-08.
editor_notes.series_e_attribution_check: Verified via targeted grep across the raw TechCrunch snapshot: the string 'series-e' occurs exactly once in the entire source-1.html.gz file, and it is the href of a link Cognition's outbound announcement URL (https://cognition.com/blog/series-e) embedded in TechCrunch's opening sentence ('...Devin, announced it raised $2 billion...') — the anchor text itself is just 'announced'. TechCrunch's own visible prose never uses the words 'Series E' anywhere in the article. By contrast, Cognition's own blog post (source-2) titles itself 'Do it all with Devin: Announcing our Series E' in its , og:title, twitter:title, and JSON-LD headline — i.e. Cognition itself is the source of the 'Series E' label. The submission's phrasing ('That round — which Cognition's own announcement titled its Series E — came just four months after...') correctly attributes the label to Cognition's blog and never claims TechCrunch used the term. This attribution claim is accurate and no misattribution to TechCrunch was found.
editor_notes.customer_lists_check: The two customer lists are kept separate and correctly attributed, not merged. The article states TechCrunch's Sept 8 list (Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, Citi) separately from Cognition's Sept 25 list (GE Aerospace, Rivian, Rohlik, Exa), explicitly noting each is from a 'separate' post. Verified both lists verbatim against their respective snapshots — TechCrunch: 'Cognition counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi among its major enterprise customers'; Cognition's blog: 'Devin works alongside engineering teams at GE Aerospace, Rivian, Rohlik, Exa, and many more.' No cross-contamination between the two lists.
editor_notes.cross_reference_check: Both internal cross-references resolve to real, accurate prior articles. (1) /article/2026-06/02-cognition-raises-1-billion-at-26-billion-valuation-as-devin-ai-engineer-hits-492-million-in-annualized-revenue exists and reports the $492M ARR / $26B (post-money, from $25B pre-money) valuation Series D — matches what the new submission cites as the May baseline. (2) /article/2026-08/17-spacex-closes-60-billion-acquisition-of-cursor-completing-the-deal-it-struck-in-june exists and confirms the $60B SpaceX-Cursor acquisition closed Aug 14, 2026 — matches the submission's Analysis-section reference.
editor_notes.financial_trajectory_check: Full trajectory verified verbatim across sources: May $492M ARR / $26B valuation (matches June article + is referenced in both Sept sources); Sept 8 $900M ('almost $900M' per Cognition, 'to $900 million' per TechCrunch) ARR / $48B valuation via $2B round (TechCrunch, Cognition both confirm); Sept 25 $1B ARR milestone (Cognition blog, dated 2026-09-25). All figures in the submission match the source text exactly.
editor_notes.misattribution_findings: Found two subordinate-claim misattributions to TechCrunch of facts TechCrunch's own article explicitly sources to The Information: (1) the submission's 'Costs' paragraph says 'TechCrunch reported that the company leases an Nvidia server cluster costing "hundreds of millions of dollars annually," which could push its total cash burn to $800 million for 2026' — but TechCrunch's actual sentence is 'Cognition leases an Nvidia server cluster that costs hundreds of millions of dollars annually, which could push its total cash burn to $800 million this year, The Information reported.' (2) the submission's 'Revenue trajectory' paragraph says 'TechCrunch also reported that Cognition was expected to reach $4 billion to $5 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026' — but TechCrunch's actual sentence is 'Cognition is expected to reach $4 billion to $5 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, according to The Information.' Both underlying facts are true and verifiably present in the TechCrunch snapshot (so not fabrications), but the attribution is to the wrong outlet in both cases — TechCrunch was itself relaying The Information's reporting, not reporting it firsthand. Both are subordinate body claims, not the headline/summary/lead (which rest on the accurately-sourced $1B ARR milestone and Series E facts). This is exactly the 'cites the wrong outlet for a real fact' case the workflow earmarks for APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS rather than REJECT.

The two related prior stories (May Series D / $492M ARR, and August SpaceX-Cursor close) are different, older events correctly cross-referenced rather than duplicated. Not a duplicate.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; attributions are hedged appropriately ('according to', 'the company wrote') except for the two misattributions noted above.
concerns: TechCrunch is credited as the source for the '$800 million' 2026 cash-burn figure and the '$4 billion to $5 billion' 2026 ARR forecast, but TechCrunch's own article attributes both figures to The Information, not to its own reporting.
cognition.com is not on config/source_allowlist.txt (used twice as a source) — a legitimate primary-source company blog, but not yet formally allowlisted.
recommendations: File a corrections record noting the two figures (the $800M 2026 cash-burn estimate and the $4-5B 2026 ARR forecast) were originally reported by The Information and only relayed by TechCrunch, not TechCrunch's own reporting.
Consider adding cognition.com to config/source_allowlist.txt given it is a recurring, legitimate primary source for company announcements.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced submission with an accurate and carefully-attributed Series E/TechCrunch distinction and correctly separated customer lists. Two subordinate facts are misattributed to TechCrunch instead of The Information (which TechCrunch itself cites) — both real, verifiable facts, both recoverable with a single corrections entry each. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
